items.title: 8.8.1 Equilibrium constant expressions of some important reactions

source_refs.note: Topic 8.8.1, printed pages 174-176, with Sample Problems 8.1 and 8.2 and Quick Check 8.4.

blocks.title: Sample Problem 8.1
blocks.problem: Ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid to form ethyl ethanoate and water. CH₃COOH(l) + C₂H₅OH(l) ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅(l) + H₂O(l) (ethanoic acid + ethanol ⇌ ethyl ethanoate + water). 500 cm³ of the reaction mixture at equilibrium contained 0.235 mol of ethanoic acid and 0.0350 mol of ethanol together with 0.182 mol of ethyl ethanoate and 0.182 mol of water. Use this data to calculate a value of Kc for this reaction.
steps: Step 1 Write out the balanced chemical equation with the concentrations beneath each substance. CH₃COOH(l): 0.235 mol / 0.5 dm³ = 0.470 mol dm⁻³; C₂H₅OH(l): 0.0350 mol / 0.5 dm³ = 0.070 mol dm⁻³; CH₃COOC₂H₅(l): 0.182 mol / 0.5 dm³ = 0.364 mol dm⁻³; H₂O(l): 0.182 mol / 0.5 dm³ = 0.364 mol dm⁻³
Step 2 Write the equilibrium constant for this reaction in terms of concentrations. Kc = [CH₃COOC₂H₅][H₂O] / [CH₃COOH][C₂H₅OH] = (0.364 mol dm⁻³)(0.0364 mol dm⁻³) / (0.470 mol dm⁻³)(0.070 mol dm⁻³)
Step 3 Substitute the equilibrium concentrations into the expression: Kc = 4.03 (to 3 significant figures)
Step 4 Add the correct units by referring back to the equilibrium expression: The units of mol dm⁻³ cancel out, so Kc has no units.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In Step 2 the water concentration is printed as 0.0364 mol dm⁻³. Step 1 gives 0.364 mol dm⁻³, and only that value gives the book's answer: Kc = (0.364 × 0.364) / (0.470 × 0.070) = 4.03.

blocks.title: Sample Problem 8.2
blocks.problem: Propanone reacts with hydrogen cyanide as follows: CH₃COCH₃(l) + HCN(g) ⇌ CH₃C(OH)(CN)CH₃(l) (propanone + hydrogen cyanide ⇌ product). A mixture of 0.0500 mol dm⁻³ propanone and 0.0500 mol dm⁻³ hydrogen cyanide is left to reach equilibrium at room temperature. At equilibrium the concentration of the product is 0.0233 mol dm⁻³. Calculate Kc for this reaction.
steps: Step 1 Write out the balanced chemical equation with all the data underneath: CH₃COCH₃(l) + HCN(g) ⇌ CH₃C(OH)(CN)CH₃(l). Initial conc.: 0.0500 mol dm⁻³, 0.0500 mol dm⁻³, 0 mol dm⁻³. Equil. conc.: ?, ?, 0.0233 mol dm⁻³.

Step 2 Calculate the equilibrium concentrations of the reactants. The chemical equation shows that for every mole of product formed, 1 mole of CH₃COCH₃ and 1 mole of HCN are consumed. So the equilibrium concentrations are as follows: CH₃COCH₃; 0.0500 – 0.0233 = 0.0267 mol dm⁻³. HCN; 0.0500 – 0.0233 = 0.0267 mol dm⁻³
Step 3 Write the equilibrium constant for this reaction in terms of concentrations: Kc = [CH₃C(OH)(CN)CH₃] / [CH₃COH₃][HCN] = (0.0233 mol dm⁻³) / (0.05 mol dm⁻³)(0.05 mol dm⁻³)
Step 4 Substitute the equilibrium concentrations into the expression

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Step 3 prints propanone as CH₃COH₃; it is CH₃COCH₃. The equilibrium concentrations from Step 2, 0.0267 mol dm⁻³ each, belong in the expression, not the starting 0.05 mol dm⁻³: Kc = 0.0233 / (0.0267 × 0.0267) = 32.7. The unit is (mol dm⁻³)⁻¹ = mol⁻¹ dm³, not mol dm⁻³.
